lines: I had a <italic>footnote</italic> for this joke, but mercy won.
I told a book joke once. It was overdue before anyone laughed.
My shelf joke has excellent support.
I tried a paper joke. It folded under pressure.
A bookmark knows exactly where to stop.
The lectern laughed at me, though only in creaks.
I know an ink joke, but it stains the conversation.
A title should not give the whole joke away.
My index points toward funnier material elsewhere.
The quietest punchline is hiding in the appendix.
I tried a history joke. Everyone had heard it before.
A library joke lands softly and expects to be returned.
I asked a book for humor. It opened to a blank page.
My best joke is rare, well bound, and constantly misplaced.
A villager asked for light reading, so I handed over the thinnest book.
The dictionary and I disagree on the meaning of a short conversation.
I wrote a joke in the margin. Now it lacks proper boundaries.
The atlas wanted to travel, but it could not get past the cover.
That punchline needs another draft and perhaps a different audience.
If nobody laughs, I can always claim it was a historical quotation.
